subject: OpenRetail renewal & expansion — request for op-exemption and price shield
messages:
From: Olivia Park <olivia@openretail.com>
To: mateo_alvarez@redwood.ai
Date: Sat, 19 Sep 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Renewal + expansion ask (Q4 start)

Hi Mateo —

Thanks again for the run last quarter — the team is seeing meaningful latency wins and cost improvements. We expect a meaningful uplift in usage starting early Q4 as we enable more internal teams. Before we ramp, procurement asked us to get renewal economics in place. Key asks from our side: 

- Temporary price shield for 3 months after renewal (we're worried about near-term spot price shifts).
- Ability to convert our current retainer credits into a committed usage bucket (we can increase commitment if needed).
- A one-time expansion credit to help offset migration work (30k-$ equivalent).
- Procurement would like an invoice deferral option for one cycle while PO gets approved.

Can you share a proposed path (numbers + timelines)? We have procurement contact Samir Shah (cc) who will review commercial terms.

Appreciate it — looking to align this week so we can start trials in October.

Best,
Olivia
Head of ML Platforms, OpenRetail

Attachments: usage_snapshot_q3.csv (stub)

From: mateo_alvarez@redwood.ai <mateo_alvarez@redwood.ai>
To: Olivia Park <olivia@openretail.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 21 Sep 2026 10:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal + expansion ask (Q4 start)

Hi Olivia —

Thanks for the clear ask and the usage snapshot. Really glad the latency gains are pay-ing off. High level proposal so we have something concrete for procurement: 

- Commitment: convert current retainer into a committed (announced) monthly spend of $85k (was $50k retainer) for the first 6 months, with a rolling true-up.
- One-time expansion credit: $25,000 applied to the first invoice after renewal.
- Temporary price shield: hold current per-token rates for 90 days post-renewal; after 90 days we'll revert to the published rate or a mutually agreed variant.
- OpEx invoice deferral: allow a single invoice deferral of up to 60 days (one-time) while PO clears — requires a signed commitment and procurement contact on the DocuSign.

I've attached a draft term sheet (openretail_term_sheet_v1.pdf) with the above spelled out and a short MAM (mutual action plan) for onboarding extra teams. If this is directionally OK I can set up a 30-min sync with procurement to walk the mechanics and get Samir's confirmation.

Questions for you/procurement:
- Is the $85k/month commitment acceptable as a starting point? We can phase it if needed (e.g., 75k for month 1–2 then 85k).
- Do you need us to waive prepayment for the first invoice (we can consider a one-time waiver but need internal approval)?

If you want, I can loop in Prioym/DAS for pricing/legal redlines — copying Marissa and Karthik to track approval flow.

Thanks,
Mateo Alvarez
Account Lead, Redwood Inference

Attachment: openretail_term_sheet_v1.pdf (term sheet stub)

From: Olivia Park <olivia@openretail.com>
To: mateo_alvarez@redwood.ai
Cc: Samir Shah <samir@openretail.com>
Date: Wed, 23 Sep 2026 08:40:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal + expansion ask (Q4 start)

Mateo —

Appreciate the quick draft. A few procurement-driven clarifications from Samir (copied):

- The $85k/month headline is OK if we can get a 3-month price shield and the one-time $25k credit applied up front.
- Procurement needs an OpEx-friendly path: can Redwood accept a 60-day invoice deferral for the first renewal invoice (we expect PO approval by then)? If not possible, can we get a structured prepayment waiver while PO is pending?
- Legal asked for a short clause that guarantees no mid-term surcharges above the shielded rate for the 90-day window.

Also: Samir asked whether we can convert the retainer credit balance to committed consumption units rather than a cash credit — that would help internal reporting.

We can sign the term-sheet in DocuSign once you add the OpEx deferral clause and indicate the credit conversion mechanics.

Olivia

On Wed, Sep 23, 2026 at 08:40 AM Samir Shah <samir@openretail.com> wrote:
> Thanks — procurement here. If Redwood can provide a one-time 60-day invoice deferral while PO processes, that removes a blocker. We'll also need a short approval from your finance or sales leadership acknowledging the exception.
> 
> Samir
> Director, Procurement, OpenRetail

From: mateo_alvarez@redwood.ai <mateo_alvarez@redwood.ai>
To: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Cc: priyom_das@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 25 Sep 2026 14:22:00 -07:00
Subject: INTERNAL: OpenRetail renewal — approval request for OpEx deferral & credit conversion

Team —

Summary of thread with OpenRetail (see HubSpot OR-4321): they want to convert their retainer into a committed spend, increase the starting commitment to $85k/month for a minimum 6-month window, and request two programmatic concessions: a one-time expansion credit ($25k) and a single-invoice OpEx deferral of 60 days while their PO clears. They also require a 90-day price shield on current published rates.

Concrete asks for internal sign-off: 
- Approve one-time prepayment waiver / OpEx deferral (60 days) for the first invoice tied to the renewal. This will require finance acknowledgement but does not change long-term terms.
- Approve application of $25k expansion credit to first invoice; credit is not refundable and will be netted against invoice.
- Approve conversion mechanics: existing retainer balance to be converted into committed consumption units at current rates; any overage billed at published rates after the shield window.

Why we should approve:
- OpenRetail is expanding across multiple teams; the uplift materially increases committed spend and provides predictable six-month revenue.
- Approving a one-time deferral reduces friction and accelerates signing.

Risks/controls:
- Require DocuSign with procurement contact Samir listed and an explicit clause limiting deferral to one invoice.
- Add an internal approval doc (approval_opEx_waiver.docx) to record finance sign-off.

Suggested next steps: 
1) Marissa — can you confirm finance is comfortable with a one-time 60-day deferral and sign the approval doc?
2) Karthik — if yes I will finalize the term sheet and send DocuSign for signatures; please note pricing shield clause and credit application mechanics.
3) Prioym — please prepare a short amendment template for the conversion and shield clause.

If we approve today I can send the DocuSign by EOD and schedule a 30-min handoff with Samir/Oliv ia.

Thanks,
Mateo
Account Lead, Redwood Inference

Attachment: approval_opEx_waiver.docx (internal approval stub)
